source_reentry.purpose: Conjunction, stale-result distinctions and gap-dependent reported value
source_reentry.read_raw_text:
### Conjunction of results

Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6). Purpose and
material relation: failure, undecidability, non-performance and uncertain
effects stay distinct after combination, so a composite can neither report
success nor hide which kind of gap it has while one of them remains in
what it requires.

A conjunction takes three inputs and keeps them apart:

1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

Stale results. A held result is stale for a composite when the basis it
binds is not the basis the composite requires of that component, because
a later state has superseded or advanced it or because it binds another
subject or basis (§2, Basis). Two questions stay apart, so that one
composite has one reported value (P3, P5, P6):

- an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
  ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
  `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
  basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
  states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
  `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
- the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
  returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
  whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
  composite basis, and which do not.

A stale `satisfied` never counts toward the composite. Purpose and
material relation: answering one stale component as a gap in one place and
as `invalid_basis` in another would give one composite two reported
values; keeping the evaluation's own value apart from the composite's gap
keeps the reported value unique and the stale result visible.

Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).

Predicates travel. Each component keeps its predicate and domain outcome
through every join, so an uncertain effect stays distinct from a failure
and from an undecided claim, and a `satisfied` for one predicate never
counts toward another: a step's `satisfied` for "a candidate is available"
never counts toward the candidate's fitness or acceptance.

Reported value. The conjunction is `satisfied` only when every mandatory
result is `satisfied` with valid applicable evidence, the declared basis
relations agree, and the second and third inputs are empty. A composite
with a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint or an uncovered
required obligation cannot project success. Where a mandatory result is
not `satisfied`, the conjunction
reports a non-satisfied value chosen by its declared rule from those
returned; no universal order among the non-satisfied values exists, and
the member or profile that applies the conjunction declares its own in
its declared rule. Where every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`
and the declared basis relations disagree, the conjunction reports
`invalid_basis`, because no coherent composite basis supports the
composite predicate (§2, Basis); any gaps stay recorded by kind. Where
every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`, the declared basis
relations agree and a gap remains, the conjunction reports
`indeterminate`, because the results it holds cannot decide the composite
predicate; that value is the conjunction's own, and the gaps stay
recorded by kind. A `falsified` result that is not mandatory stays in the
conjunction's record with its predicate and is never discarded. Where
every mandatory result is `satisfied`, the declared basis relations agree
and no gap remains, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint
falsifies the conjunction whichever contributor found it, and without one
the conjunction's value is the one its declared rule gives over the
mandatory results.

The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

Composition of results. The result of composed steps for the outer
predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
`satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
Refinement).

source_reentry.read_raw_text:
### Applicability

The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame
obligations apply to the exact subject. Their declared predicates are
evaluated from sufficient basis-bound facts: a true predicate requires the
applicable evaluation and its result; a false predicate excludes only that
obligation, under its cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise
leaves applicability unresolved, not false. A supported inapplicability
of a conditional obligation is recorded as such, apart from any result
value, and waives no criterion of the member's acceptance (P5, P6). A frame name, an available
tool or a listed family triggers no activation by itself. Where
applicability needs residual semantic judgment, that judgment and its
evidence are retained as a judgment, never represented as a computed fact
(P6, P1). A required result that is absent, stale, bound to another subject
or basis, or incapable of establishing its claim cannot satisfy a dependent
conjunction ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
unresolved applicability withholds the dependent claim until
sufficient evidence or the owning decision resolves it; other applicable
constraints stay in force even if only one evaluation detects them (P4b,
P5). Qualification of an applicability rule distinguishes true, false and
unknown premises, required results that are missing or bound to the wrong
subject, and a sufficient positive result, under a finite declared fixture;
a rule that always skips or always activates cannot satisfy those distinct
expected outcomes (EVALUATION §7).

Exclusion and the core. Deciding applicability is an evaluation of the
predicate "the obligation applies to the exact subject", and its result is
a core value of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): a true
predicate is `satisfied`; a false predicate is `falsified`, the
basis-bound fact that makes it false being the counterexample; a missing
or ambiguous premise is `indeterminate`, or `out_of_frame` where the
premise needs a relation the frame does not declare, and never
`falsified`. An exclusion is the state of the excluded obligation after a
`falsified` applicability result: it is no result, the obligation's own
evaluation is not performed and maps to no core value, and the obligation
leaves the required coverage of a dependent conjunction under the cited
authority of that applicability result. An obligation whose applicability is
unresolved stays in that required coverage. A predicate that its owner
declares as a disjunction that includes non-application, such as "meets
the axiom or does not apply", may be `satisfied` because the obligation
does not apply; that `satisfied` is for the declared disjunction only and
never counts toward the predicate that the obligation holds
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Predicates travel). Members, profiles and projects refer to this
paragraph for exclusions and do not decide them again (P5, P6, P1).
Purpose and material relation: an exclusion read as a result of the
excluded obligation, or a "does not apply" counted toward that obligation,
would report a skipped obligation as met; an unresolved premise read as an
exclusion would drop an obligation that may apply.

source_reentry.purpose: Effect value versus independently unresolved end
source_reentry.read_raw_text:
### Effects

An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
premise, P6):

| Value | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
| `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
| `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |

`not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
`completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.

Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
`not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
`not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).

An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
while its end is not established.

The refinement's material relation is whether an action whose
external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
effect that may still be acting.

source_reentry.purpose: Current workspace and actor account on resume
source_reentry.read_raw_text:
### The workspace and an actor's account

The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
material state decides what the work has and has not done. An actor's
context is an account of that state. It is bounded, because it is a
projection of the state (§2); revisable, because an observation can
correct it; and disposable, because a step records its closed results and
step-produced facts before it returns (§1 Admission; P4b). An account is
never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
it (§1 Intake) (P0, P3, P6).

Acquisition ([§2](#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)) observes the
current subject and its authoritative inputs. Where they materially
disagree with a cached belief, a retained summary or a prior result, the
actor reconciles the disagreement: current evidence corrects the account,
and what the evidence cannot decide stays an explicit unknown. A stored
belief, a summary or a successful prior result never overrules contrary
current evidence. A prior result is relied on only after its
applicability and invalidators are checked against the current subject
and inputs (§7). The actor corrects its account within its grant; where
resolving the disagreement needs an operation, a territory or a decision
outside the grant, the step stops with `re_entry_requested(authority)`,
naming the owner of what it needs (§3 Construction availability) (P5,
P6).

Discarding an actor's private context resets nothing: the workspace, the
applicable valid work and the outstanding obligations remain as the work
state records them. A missing trace in a context, a memory or a summary is
no evidence about the subject. It shows neither that work was not done
nor that an external effect did not occur, nor that it ended; an effect
of uncertain completion keeps the value `completion_unknown`, or its end
stays not established beside its `not_effected` value, until evidence
about the subject decides it (§3 Effects) (P5).

Work that an interruption left partly written is part of the current
material state from which resumption (above) starts, and is assessed as
it stands; an assessment that was not performed has no result and is
never recorded as performed
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); §3 Construction
availability). The method imposes no universal reset and no obligation to
replay the complete history. The recovery contract that applies, which is
the resuming step's intake with the work state, determines which
observations and which effect reconciliations the next dependent action
needs. Handoff between actors is by closed results, which carry no private
working context and keep their validity and independence conditions (§7)
(P0, P4b).

Purpose and material relation: finite context (P0) means an actor's
context ends or is replaced while the work continues, and discarding it is
safe only because the step-produced facts the outer contract needs are
recorded (P4b). Treating the account as the truth surface would let a
stale account overrule the workspace; treating a discarded account as a
reset would erase progress or repeat an effect that occurred (P5, P6). The
material relation is whether a decision relies on an account that current
evidence contradicts, or reads a missing record as undone work or an
absent effect.  The workspace, the
work state and the closed results carry it, and no further carrier is
required.

source_reentry.read_raw_text:
## 7. Closed result and reuse

A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
uncertainty and the invalidation conditions (the minimal shape is
REFERENCE_FRAME §13). The frame's internal working context need not be
transferred when the closed result and its provenance are sufficient for
the consuming decision; it may still be attached, for audit or otherwise,
without changing the result. Independent evaluations may share valid
mechanical evidence under the declared independence conditions of
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), which owns that
permission (P4b, P0).

The selection of affected results after a change and the conditions for
retaining evidence on a new subject are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse);
this section applies them to closed results and handoffs, and the three
invalidators below are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected
when its dependencies `D*(t)` meet the impact cover `I(Δ)` (P3, P6).

A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer that checks exact
applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates
nothing. An invalidator invalidates the affected result before reliance,
even where the subject's own bytes are unchanged, preserving its
predecessor/successor relation and any demonstrably independent surviving
results. Invalidation withdraws the result from direct reliance; whether
its evidence is retained on the new basis is decided by `retain_applicable`
of FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse, and the changed
coordinate alone establishes neither that the claim fails nor that it
holds. The invalidators are three:

- a material input change: a change to the result's subject or to an
  input it rests on, including the admissible evidence that bears on its
  predicate; newly acquired or changed admissible evidence is such a
  change when it is material to the result as
  [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines material, that is,
  when it could change the result's value;
- a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
  binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
- a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
  judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.

A changed source, task or actor condition is a changed basis where the
basis binds it, and otherwise a material input change; a role change that
alters a required actor condition is such a change, while a role,
conversation or resumption change that alters none of these invalidates
nothing (P3, P6).

Judgment continuity names the basis and the evidence; Return A Closed
Result names inputs and the observation. A member, profile or project
that names a trigger for its own domain, such as a changed projection,
rule or configuration, names it as an instance of one of these three and
states no parallel list (P3, P4b, P6). A reused judgment does not
satisfy a separately required independent judgment; the independent assessor
acquires its own evidence and supplies its own judgment. [TICKETS §7](TICKETS.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity)
uses the same evidence invalidator. Naming these kinds once gives every
consumer the same triggers. The
material relation is whether a result is relied on after a change that
could alter it (P3, P6). Whether a revision of a frame needs a new
revision coordinate is
[REFERENCE_FRAME §10](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#revision-actions)'s question;
whether a result it touches stays valid is this section's.

source_reentry.read_raw_text:
### Condition-based closure and reuse

A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains. A mandatory obligation whose applicability is
unknown, or whose evidence is insufficient, withholds the dependent claim;
evidence presence alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any
reserved acceptance (P6, P5).
This condition is the
[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) with the
declared obligations as required coverage. This section owns the
closure condition of a work claim;
[SPEC_METHOD §4 Consistency gate](SPEC_METHOD.md#consistency-gate)
applies it as the gate over a declared change span.

Review evaluates these conditions; its occurrence is not the closing event.
Where applicable law requires no independent review or reserved
acceptance, a work claim is recorded as
[ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)
states in Recording a result without review, with the ticket as the
existing carrier. The conditions that still apply include sprint-close
law (§3) and the design profile's law (P6, P2).

An unchanged obligation reuses valid applicable evidence and recorded J
and O under the reuse rule of
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse). For a work
claim, the changed material inputs and revising observations that rule
names include a material counterexample, changed evidence and a stated
revising observation of a recorded J; with a changed basis, each
invalidates the affected claim and its dependent results before further
reliance. An unrelated observation is retained as bounded repricing input;
it does not reopen a satisfied claim or expand the work automatically.
Closure recording preserves the exact evaluated scope, the satisfied
conditions, the evidence and the remaining residuals (P4b, P2).


Goals define the current overriding concerns for the active body of work.
Intent defines purpose and direction. Product Definition defines the current
product realisation of the mutable source project, its key terms and its
end-state shape in terms that can be decomposed into requirements.
Requirements define invariant truths the system must satisfy. Design
defines the structural decisions, interfaces, carrier surfaces and delivery
topology that make those truths achievable; ADRs are one durable form of
design record, not a second constitutional layer above design. Code
realises those decisions where the selected execution environment is
software; a performed human procedure realises them where it is a human
process, and both where it is mixed (§11). Events are the retained
record of what happened, in the carrier the binding selects: an event
stream, a ledger, a signed record or an observation log. Projection
reconstructs current truth from that retained record where the record is
sufficient for the product's obligations; it need not replay a complete
event stream. Delta reveals drift
between intended truth and realised state. Scenarios test operational
meaning: whether the system can do what the words describe. Gap analysis
identifies where real use cases hit the current model and reveal
insufficiency. Repricing updates goals, intent, product, requirements,
design or code when the system no longer harmonises; when gap analysis
reveals constitutional insufficiency, repricing re-enters at the layer its
[change class](#change-classes) names and generates new goals or intent
where the work wave, direction or scope changes (P2, P1).

This is the homeostatic loop. Every link is load-bearing. A break at any
link, goals with no downstream repricing path, an unowned requirement, an
ungrounded design record, code without a design decision, creates
accidental law (P6). Load-bearing means owned, not software: the links
Code, Events and Projection name responsibilities every realisation
carries in the carrier its binding selects (§11), and no product owes a
code base or an event store that its binding does not select (P2, P6).

The goals surface is the bounded work-wave surface: it captures the current
overriding concerns for the next body of work, keeps temporary focus out of
deeper constitutional layers until it is intentionally repriced there, and
is more immediate than intent while remaining higher-level than product
definition and requirements. The product-definition surface is the bridge
between direction and obligation: it states the current product definition
of the mutable source project in present-tense terms, names the product
terms and boundaries that downstream layers rely on, and provides the
surface that requirements decompose. It is not the immutable release cut
and not the installed product; those are the lineage objects of FOUNDATIONS
§2 (P3).

Requirements are the constitutional what of the project. They are not
limited to user-visible features: the live requirement surface may include
capabilities, invariants, constraints, governance and verification
obligations; what matters is that each requirement states something the
project must make true. Design is the structural how: it chooses the
concrete realisation that satisfies requirement truth, interfaces, topology,
file placement, carrier documents, entry and control surfaces, runtime
wiring and lawful tenant boundaries. Requirements may require such surfaces
to exist and be delivered; design chooses where and how they are realised
unless the path itself is constitutional (P2, P1).

## 11. Build-tenant binding

This section owns the relation between a product's WHAT and the build
tenants that realise it: what a tenant binds, what stays fixed while it
chooses, and what its evidence shows. It applies to every product built
with this method (P2, P1, P6).

Terms used in this section:

- A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a
  product's WHAT. The build-tenancy context of
  [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#8-what-how-and-work-carriers)
  names it, and the product definition's tenant registry locates each one.
- The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its
  WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and
  composing the work that realises it.
- A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,
  with the laws by which they compose, the transformations they permit,
  and their effects and resource behaviour, as far as these are material
  to the obligations.
- An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those
  operations: a technology stack; a human process, made of people, roles,
  documents, communication channels and decision procedures; or a
  combination of the two.
- A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts: its calculus binding,
  from the requirements calculus to its computational calculus, and its
  execution binding, from that computational calculus to its execution
  environment. A tenant's registry entry locates the tenant; it is not the
  binding.
- A generic procedure is a method procedure whose scope is independent of
  the selected execution environment. It and its projections preserve the
  bindings Rule 2 permits: code, an event stream or reconstruction from a
  complete history is required only where the governing obligations or
  the selected execution binding require it, and an adequate human
  process using current records and direct observation is a permitted
  execution binding of a generic procedure that requires none of them
  (P1, P6).
- Author identity and actor identity are as
  [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) defines them:
  authorship is one condition of an assessment's independence there, and
  an actor's identity is not an authority.
  Operation kind is what an operation does, such as construct, assess,
  relay, record, measure or decide, together with the authority that kind
  of operation requires.

Rules:

1. Realisations of one WHAT. One WHAT is realised by one or more
   independent build tenants, whatever the physical layout. The WHAT is
   constitutional and each tenant's realisation is HOW; a tenant-local
   realisation stays derivative until its governing truth is ratified in
   specification (§2). Each tenant binds the product's requirements
   calculus to a declared computational calculus and binds that calculus
   to a concrete execution environment. Both bindings are that tenant's
   design and realisation: they are declared in its existing design and
   realisation surfaces, chosen under the Design rule (§2) and recorded as
   design decisions (§10), and the method requires no further carrier. The
   tenant owns its binding, its realisation and their evidence; the WHAT
   keeps its meaning (P2, P6).
2. Selection. The execution environment may be a technology stack, a
   human process or a combination. Its selection stays within the
   requirements calculus, including every human decision that calculus
   requires: no choice of environment removes a required human decision or
   a required independent assessment. Author identity, actor identity and
   operation kind stay distinct, and none determines another. Who authored
   a tenant does not select its environment; one actor may perform
   operations of several kinds, each under its own grant; and an actor's
   identity neither decides the kind of an operation nor grants authority
   for it. A person performing an operation does not by that make it human
   adjudication: §5 states the admission that makes an operation human
   adjudication and how a person who decides under policy without it is
   governed. The same holds for every decision the requirements reserve to
   a human: the person the governing authority admits for it takes it, and
   a person's part elsewhere in the process does not (P6, P1).
3. Material content. For the obligations it serves, the binding
   identifies:
   - the operations, each with its inputs, outputs, effects and outcome
     values; each outcome value maps to exactly one core value under
     [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), and an intended
     external effect, one of uncertain completion included, is recorded as
     [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) states;
   - the composition laws, and the transformations the calculus permits;
   - the resource measures;
   - the operational assumptions on which conformance depends, among them
     those about actors, tools, availability and failure.

   Human effort, elapsed time, communication and machine resources are
   measured where a selected obligation needs them. Each measure states its
   unit and its boundary: what is counted, and where measurement starts and
   stops. A resource claim without its unit or its boundary supports no
   conformance claim. The size of a selected context is measured as
   [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)
   step 3 measures it, against the capacity the binding declares for the
   actor. The law for declaring, measuring and honouring resource limits
   is [ACTIVATION §6 Resource limits](ACTIVATION.md#resource-limits), and
   this rule binds it: the values of a step's time, spend and other
   resource limits, and the units and boundaries the environment can
   measure, are those of the execution binding, stated before the
   activation they limit. Where a configuration states its resource limits
   and its assumptions about failure
   ([ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration)), it takes
   them from this binding (P0, P2, P5).
4. Conformance evidence. The obligations of the requirements calculus
   decide fitness; the kind of executor alone neither accepts nor rejects a
   realisation. Evidence establishes how the bound realisation satisfies
   the required meaning and constraints, including the applicable
   authority, independence, failure and recovery conditions. Conformance is
   judged under
   [EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations), and two
   conforming tenants need not behave identically outside the contract.
   Each assessment returns a core value for its predicate, and the tenant's
   conformance is their
   [conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results), with the
   obligations of the requirements calculus as its required coverage. A
   convenient stack never weakens an obligation. An execution plan that
   merges two required independent assessments, or substitutes an
   automated result for a required human decision, is a counterexample to
   the obligation it weakens, so the binding's conformance for that
   obligation is `falsified`; in any run under such a plan the lost
   assessment or decision has no applicable closed result. Matching

## 3. Independent assessment

A constructor's self-review is construction output, not assessment. Where
promotion needs independent assessment, the assessor evaluates the exact
live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not the
constructor's summary (P6, and P0 with its premise that a step's output is
a candidate until evaluated; instance premise (c) of §1 Foundation to law).
This section decides what counts as independent assessment. Which
boundaries require it is a policy choice of the Spec Method, owned by
[TICKETS §7 Execution and verification authority separation](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
a governing basis may add boundaries.

Protocol: where method qualification applies
([§7 Method self-qualification](#method-self-qualification)), the subject is
frozen by identity before material reference exposure; elsewhere it is
stabilised by an immutable identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation
sufficient for the claimed assessment. The assessor records its
expectations from the governing source before opening the candidate; it
reads the subject at that identity or relation, never a mutable working
tree; it makes no repair; it does not assess its
own authorship. Reusing the constructor's judgment does not satisfy
independence; shared mechanical evidence may be reused, judgment may not
(ACTIVATION §7). Binding a returned assessment to its producer, subject,
basis and evidence authenticates the result; it establishes neither the
assertion provenance of its expected answer nor the execution provenance
of its run, which
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
requires separately (P6, P3). Membership in a plan authenticates nothing,
an unauthenticated result satisfies no required assessment, and a result
bound to another subject satisfies no planned assessment
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
no cryptographic or transport protocol is prescribed for the binding (P6). Any post-exposure revision is a declared intervention: it
is either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new
qualification subject, and it cannot retroactively make the original
frozen construction pass. This law prescribes no actor type or count,
review-round count, engine, prompt or orchestration (P6).

Author identity is the party responsible for the content of a realised
subject. It is distinct from actor identity, whoever performs one
operation, which is an identity and not an authority
([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)).
Authorship is one of the conditions on
which the independence of an assessment rests; the evidence conditions are
the other (P6, P3).

Reporting a defect, supplying a counterexample or identifying behaviour
already required by governing law does not by itself author the realised
subject. Contributing wording, design or policy that is adopted into the
subject, including through directions for a particular repair, is authorship
of that contribution. A
reporter may assess a later repair only when the existing assessment grant,
authorship relation and evidence-independence conditions permit it; a
reporter gains no review authority from having found the defect. A person
who authored an adopted repair cannot supply its required independent
assessment by calling that authorship a finding (P6, P3).

Independence rests on authorship and on the evidence conditions above, not
on a new context. The assessor may read the same governing sources as the
constructor. A fresh context alone establishes no independence, and it
supplies no review authority the author lacks: an author that opens a
fresh context to review its own candidate is still its author, and its
review is self-review, which stays construction output and cannot be
relabelled as independent assessment (P6;
[TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007)). A contribution received from another author stays that
author's wherever it is carried, and that author's reading of it supplies
no independent acceptance of it (P6).

Independence across actor families is declared, not assumed. Whether two
activations of one model family are independent for a semantic judgment is a
policy the governing basis states for the claim; the default where it is not
stated is that they are not independent.

## 1. The boundary

The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor. Terms owned outside
the core, by a profile or a realisation, never enter tier 1 or 2: graph, edge, vector, ledger, event
log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, and the design
profile's IACS and Prime. The traversal record and the functor kinds F_D,
F_P and F_H are tier-1 calculus terms owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5, and
"module" is a generic term under [ASSURANCE](ASSURANCE.md); neither is
restricted here. A profile may bind a core mechanism to one of these;
the binding is declared in the profile with its direction, preserved
meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. In this member "binding" means
that declared binding of a core mechanism; a Product's adoption binding is
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)'s,
and a carrier binding to a typed contract is [UX §7](UX.md#7-carrier-binding)'s;
the three are not interchanged (P0 boundary, P1). A concrete application
of the declared-binding rule is ODD's specialisation of F_P and F_H, which
[ODD §5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute) owns in the
graph-native context.

Import rule. A profile imports the generic families of tiers 1 and 2 that
its rules rest on, and owns only its own bindings: the terms and choices
it adds for its domain or operation, among them the declared bindings
above (P1, P6). It imports each concept it uses from a member of tiers 1
and 2 under
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members),
which states what an import is, and restates none of that member's rules.
Its family table, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
names each imported family by its ID and the section that holds its table,
in the premise column; the profile's rules rest on that family's
consequences, with the standing FOUNDATIONS §3 gives them, and the
family's rules and choices keep their owners. A profile that refines
another profile declares the refinement in its lead; the refined profile
keeps its rules, and the refining profile owns only what it adds (P1, P6).
Purpose and material relation:
each profile table cites the families it rests on without restating them,
so no generic rule gains a second owner in a profile and no choice a
profile adds is presented as following from the foundations (P6, P1).

A worked application, a hello world or a data mapper is an external test
subject; its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by
precedent.

## 9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

Tools discover `stdo_*.json` recursively within the selected workspace
boundary: definitions at the workspace root and definitions at arbitrarily
deep nested project roots (P3).

For a requested Product scope exactly one applicable definition is
selected; zero or several unresolved definitions fail closed, and a
symlinked definition is refused (P6, P5).

Directory nesting creates no implicit inheritance, ownership, composition
or constitutional override. Parent and child definitions stay independent
until `composition` explicitly relates them. Each composition entry records
(P6, P3):

- `product_definition`: the current locator for the target definition;
- `target_definition_id`: the stable identity expected from the target's
  `product.definition_id`;
- `relation`: the authority defining the directed composition kind, the
  source and target roles, owner, scope, lifecycle and invalidation
  conditions; and
- `contracts`: one or more exact interface, capability, identity,
  lifecycle, data, evidence or other governing contract references
  consumed by that relation.

Resolution verifies both the locator and the expected identity. Moving a
definition requires a locator update and does not change its identity.
Replacing the content at the same locator with another definition identity
fails closed. When an edge binds exact immutable Product or release
versions, the cited relation and contracts also carry and verify those
identities; the mutable definition identity cannot substitute for them
(P3, P5).

A conforming discovered set satisfies all of the following (P3, P6, P1):

- every definition validates against its selected released schema;
- every required URI and fragment resolves under the declared workspace
  and resolver boundary;
- every `product.definition_id` is unique;
- every build-tenant identity is unique within its overlay;
- every governed scope has a resolvable applicable reference-frame basis,
  and overlapping basis bindings are reconciled by their cited authority;
- every local disambiguation binds one exact term, target context,
  complete material candidate set, selected concept, authority, basis and
  scope; `resolves_to` is a member of `disambiguates`; and its referenced
  resolution carrier is congruent with those bindings;
- every material cross-context term seam resolves through an explicit
  import, disambiguation, translation or equivalence relation rather than
  nominal match;
- every composition target resolves to another product definition whose
  `product.definition_id` equals `target_definition_id`, and every
  relation and non-empty contract set resolves; and
- no two carriers claim authority for the same Product, tenant, ticket
  state or constitutional relation.

Portable Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema validation establishes structural shape.
The schema's `uri` and `uri-reference` formats are annotations unless the
declared validator implements format assertion. Conformance therefore
performs an explicit RFC 3986 URI and URI-reference syntax check with an
assertion-capable validator, followed separately by resolution, fragment
existence, selected-release identity, uniqueness across files,
constitutional sufficiency, semantic-resolution and cross-context-relation
completeness, and authority-congruence checks. The structural subset and
the semantic subset of these checks are distinct claims (EVALUATION §2;
P1, P6).

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies deterministic evaluation or proof over declared
  properties. It returns a judgment and does not perform the domain
  construction being judged (P6).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).

### AC-015 Functor classification

Every functor application binds exactly one functor kind and one traversal
identity. Applying any `F_*` kind without the bracketed traversal identity
`[v]` is incomplete (P3). Such an
application violates this law, and its outcome is `refusal(constraint)`
under AC-007; this sense of incomplete is not the construction-availability
value `incomplete` of a step
([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)). Purpose and
material relation: an application without its traversal has one core
value, and the shared word does not let it be read as a step's stop (P5).

### AC-016 Typed composition

Two traversals compose only when the first result type and judgment
satisfy the second traversal's exact domain and preconditions (P4a):

```text
F_K2[w] compose F_K1[v]
```

Composition retains both traversal identities, intermediate results,
judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. It cannot
flatten probabilistic proposal, deterministic evaluation and human
decision into one undifferentiated operation. `a_c` prescribes no
universal `F_P -> F_D -> F_H` sequence; each application owns its lawful
topology (P4a, P4b, P6). FOUNDATIONS §3 P4a consumes this law.

### Universal intake triage

There is one front door for substantive change. The intake label does not
determine the process class: a reported bug, feature request, issue,
regression, operator finding, release blocker or scenario failure all enter
through the same intake triage (P2, P6).

Intake triage determines six things: whether the report represents a
substantive change at all; the affected product boundary and intended
scope; the lawful change class; the lawful re-entry point into the
constitutional chain; the downstream surfaces and evidence that must be
repriced, re-derived or re-proved, a determination whose evidence part is
the selection `S_Δ` over the impact cover `I(Δ)` of the affected surfaces
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse));
and whether the work remains within the
currently declared release scope or requires repricing of that release
plan. No bug, feature, issue or other intake bypasses this triage by going
straight to code, tests or release handling. The purpose is not a separate
tracking bureaucracy; it is to classify impact correctly so the change
enters the method at the right constitutional boundary.

Triage diagnoses among the four causes of
[ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation),
a defective realisation, an inadequate governing requirement or design, an
inaccurate predictive model, and insufficient observation, and routes each
supported repair to the owner of its cause rather than inferring it from
the intake label; severity and priority follow the policies that
[TICKETS](TICKETS.md) owns; a bug list projects existing work state. This
paragraph applies ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis and states no
second relation (P2, P6).

Triage triangulates a failure across the applicable reference frames over
the same subject and basis. Each frame tests candidate diagnoses against
its material workspace variables, governing relations and evidence; their
combined results constrain the supported cause, preserve unresolved
alternatives and uncertainty, and identify the smallest sufficient lawful
scope of repair. The frame that exposes a failure need not contain its
cause. Repeating the same analysis under different frame names supplies no
additional causal evidence. The smallest sufficient applicable frame
configuration is used, under frame applicability and frames in conjunction
(REFERENCE_FRAME §5 and §6). The frames' results combine under the one
[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results): each
keeps the diagnosis it evaluated as its predicate, a counterexample that
one frame finds survives the join, and a frame planned and not applied
leaves its diagnosis open, never ruled out. Counterexample localisation
applies where required (ASSURANCE). This prescribes no reviewer count and no new
review round; required independence stays intact. A diagnosis grants no
repair effects and does not establish that governing meaning must change: a
candidate may instead need correction under sufficient existing law (P6).

### Change classes

The minimum lawful change classes, each with its re-entry point and the
layers its repricing flows through (P4b, P2):

| Class | Change | Re-enters at | Flows through |
|---|---|---|---|
| `goal_reprice` | current bounded work-wave focus changes | Goals | Intent, Product, Requirements, Design, Code and Evidence where that focus changes deeper constitutional truth |
| `intent_reprice` | directional or scope change | Intent | Product, Requirements, Design, Code, Evidence |
| `product_reprice` | current product realisation changes while directional intent stays stable | Product | Requirements, Design, Code, Evidence |
| `requirement_reprice` | constitutional truth changes while project direction stays stable | Requirements | Design, Code, Evidence |
| `design_reframe` | realisation structure changes while active intent and requirement truth stay stable | Design | Code, Evidence |
| `realization_refactor` | local code, configuration or attribute change with no intended constitutional or structural change | the realised surface only | nothing upstream; it must prove no upstream drift |

Smaller changes may re-enter below Goals only if they explicitly assert
that no upstream constitutional surface is changing. The absence of a
declared change class is process drift. A changed governing relation is
accepted only at its owner; accepting it inside the acting frame is a
violation whatever the size of the delta (ACTIVATION §1).
Triage records the change intent, the class, the re-entry point and when
triage occurred, wherever substantive work begins.
[TICKETS §4](TICKETS.md#change-class) records the class on the carrier.

The change classes are declared states of a change that intake triage
records, not results, and map to no core value. An evaluation that reads
a declared class returns its own core value with its predicate under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A close classification
of [TICKETS §3](TICKETS.md#close-review) that names a layer, such as
`design_reframe`, is a result for its own predicate, mapped there, and
carries the class at which the work re-enters as its domain outcome.
Purpose and material relation: a declared class is never combined as an
evaluation result, so a change classed `realization_refactor` cannot stand
in for a `satisfied` result that no upstream drift occurred (P5, P1).

### Proportional design sequencing

For one governed boundary `B`, let `M(B)` be its complete material-relation
set (decision-complete symbolic design, below) and `U(B)` the unresolved
members of that set (P2, P0):

```text
U(B) = unresolved(M(B))
decision_complete(B) iff
  U(B) = empty
  and M(B) is jointly satisfiable
  and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the
      governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations
co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B)
design_gate(B) =
  the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish
  decision_complete(B)
```

Design sequencing follows `decision_complete(B)`, not one global authoring
order (P2, P6). Co-evolution is lawful only when `decision_complete(B)` holds:
design still owns the structural HOW, but design, implementation and tests
may evolve together and reconcile before promotion or closure.
Design-gated sequencing is required when implementation would otherwise
establish an unresolved or contradictory relation, or choose between
materially non-equivalent networks, with durable consequences for future
change: the affected design decision is accepted before retained
implementation establishes it. A disposable spike may supply evidence
without becoming the selected design.

Neither mode is the global default; the same proportionality relation
selects between them. Proportionality decides which relations are material
and bounds the smallest affected gate; decision completeness is the
resulting admissibility test (ACTIVATION §6). Where a bounded symbolic
model can contract the material semantic alternatives within effective
reasoning capacity, the code, runtime-state, test, review and
reconciliation space it removes is counterfactual evidence of that
contraction, not an independent reason for a design gate. Where no
material alternative remains, a separate prior gate adds ceremony without
disambiguation (P2).

The bidirectional design-and-implementation relation is an evidence
relation, not bidirectional semantic authority. Implementation may provide
a counterexample, falsify a constraint or expose hidden ambiguity. It may
not select the missing semantic answer, rewrite upstream truth to legalise
itself, or ratify a material design decision after establishing it (P6).

The selected relation and its basis belong in the existing work or design
carrier; this rule requires no separate artifact. If implementation
exposes previously hidden architectural ambiguity, the boundary switches to
design-gated sequencing at the smallest causally closed affected decision
set rather than retroactively invalidating unrelated work. Serial
implementation repairs do not establish design acceptance. Repeated or
cross-cutting material surprises are evidence for diagnosis under
[ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation),
not a diagnosis. Where the diagnosis establishes that the affected design
cut is underconstrained, so that `decision_complete(B)` fails, one bounded
`design_reframe` follows (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes), and retained code
remains provisional evidence until that reframe is accepted. Where the
accepted design is decision-complete and the realisation alone deviates
from it, the repair is a `realization_refactor`, however often the surprise
recurs (P6, P2).

This applies the governing proportionality law: a prior design gate is
warranted when it removes material semantic ambiguity whose alternatives
would establish materially different durable architecture, and that
contraction justifies its reasoning load. It is disproportionate when
upstream truth leaves no materially divergent architecture to adjudicate
and a separate prior acceptance would add no disambiguation. Design still
records and owns the resulting HOW before promotion or closure (P2, P6).

### Decision-complete symbolic design

For one governed boundary `B`, the complete material-relation set is (P1,
P2):

```text
M(B) =
  entities + identities + relationships + cardinalities + invariants
  + authorities + authority transitions + functions
  + higher-order composition laws + topology
  + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts
  + externally observable Product meaning
  + declared domains and admission conditions
  + failure and refusal routes + effect and closure laws
  + projections + module mappings + material algorithmic obligations
```

A design boundary is decision-complete when `U(B)` is empty, `M(B)` forms
one jointly satisfiable constraint network, and every network admitted by
`M(B)` is semantically equivalent under the governing Product,
requirements and accepted design relations. This is the design gate's
acceptance criterion: a boundary is ready for retained implementation
without a prior gate exactly when it is decision-complete, and a gate that
cannot reach decision completeness has not closed (P2, P6).

Ontology, Prime contraction, IACS, target design, the domain, sequence and
state views, public contracts, module boundaries, implementation and tests
are projections of that one network at different reasoning altitudes.
Their presence, section names, individual plausibility or mechanical
validity does not establish decision completeness (P1, EVALUATION §1).

The boundary is underconstrained whenever `decision_complete(B)` is false,
including when implementation has to introduce a new material semantic
decision, projections contradict one another, or two materially
non-equivalent networks remain admissible. Local algorithm and layout
choices may remain open only when every admitted choice is semantically
equivalent under the accepted network. Contradictory projections make the
design unsatisfiable and block promotion (P1, P5): an unsatisfiable design
fails the design gate's acceptance criterion, so this block is a
precondition of the gate (§7 Gate and retrospective work), not a decision
on a review finding. Decision completeness
does not require another document: the constraint network may be expressed
through the existing Ontology, algebra, module mapping and views when those
surfaces jointly carry the complete relation (P2).

### Transformation admission completeness (UP-016)

The authority matrix names who admits; it does not by itself establish the
relation that decides which candidate transformation becomes durable
entity truth. Two designs can complete the matrix plausibly and still leave
two materially different ways to admit the same transformation (P6, P4b).

For every consequential entity-transition domain, design evidence contains
the complete transformation-admission relation over entity identity,
predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision
cardinality, admission predicate, resulting durable fact and supersession
law, through the authority matrix or an equivalent closed representation
(P6, P4b):

| Entity transition domain | Predecessor basis | Candidate family | Admission relation | Durable result | Competing-path disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

For every material admission relation, accepted design declares, in one
compact relation or equivalent representation (P6, P4b, P3):

- each admission owner and supported admission boundary;
- the exact admission-valid basis identity, predecessor and currentness
  continuity through admission, and any equal or coherent composite
  multi-owner basis;
- the complete enclosing relation, participant identities and equality
  joins;
- refusal and effect boundaries;
- the complete semantic commit unit and its decomposability: every
  materially distinct post-validation commit or publication boundary
  capable of exposing a subset, or a design-declared dominance or
  equivalence proof that named representative observations cover the
  complete partial-failure surface;
- reconstruction and the supported direct, composite and nested forms; and
- competing-path disposition.

The declaration binds the admission and standing-test semantics of
ACTIVATION §4 (Complete enclosing-relation admission; Standing structural
qualification), which solely owns them. Qualification is instantiated per
owner and supported boundary. Unsupported composite or nested forms use
`not_applicable` only when accepted domain or design excludes the form and
the boundary has no weaker or competing admission path (P6, P4b). This
obligation is false if a field, owner or supported boundary is missing or
invented downstream; if basis continuity, partial-failure boundary
coverage or its dominance or equivalence proof, or reconstruction is left
to implementation inference; or if non-applicability is established only
by a parser, helper or manufactured refusal.

### Recursive Prime and root conservation (UP-003)

At a material semantic boundary, Prime contraction applies to each
candidate semantic atom and then to the complete family produced by those
contractions. A locally irreducible atom is not globally Prime when the
family duplicates identity, authority, function, lifecycle, topology,
effect or projection meaning. Local Prime-conformance of realisation units
does not prove the semantic family globally Prime (P3, P6).

Contraction preserves root authority and every retained semantic relation.
Reducing files, functions, operations or authoring surfaces cannot
compensate for introducing another authority source or truth path (P6,
P4b). Prime evidence states the complete candidate semantic-atom family;
each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, admitted domain and
falsification condition; the whole-family contraction relation; retained
meaning and authority before and after contraction; accepted loss; and the
explicit total mapping from every proposed realisation projection to its
accepted atom or atoms (P4b, FOUNDATIONS §4 Conservation accounting). Work
inside an accepted boundary cites the existing Prime basis rather than
recreating it (P2).

### Ontology projection

The Ontology is one semantic truth (P1, P6).
These preserve it and do not become independent semantic authorities:
class or domain diagrams; sequence diagrams; state and lifecycle diagrams;
authority and effect matrices; the IACS; public APIs, operation registers,
SDK and CLI surfaces; schemas, codecs, manifests and generated catalogues;
target architecture and module design; implementation modules through
accepted target design; and test and proof inventories through
requirements and accepted design.

Each design projection identifies its Ontology source and the identity,
relationship, lifecycle, authority, function or effect law it preserves.
Any intentional omission or flattening declares accepted loss and a
failure condition (FOUNDATIONS §4 Reference versus body). Target design
may add structural HOW absent from the Ontology, but it may not originate
rival semantic meaning. Implementation and tests trace through that
accepted design rather than bypassing it (P1, P6).

If a public operation, sequence message, state transition, carrier or
effect cannot be traced through accepted design to the accepted Ontology,
it is ungrounded design and does not enter the active product line. An
implementation branch or test expectation traces to requirements plus
accepted design; it preserves, but need not be enumerated by, the
Ontology (P6; SPEC_METHOD §2 Trace closure and anti-drift).

### Invariant reconstruction sufficiency (UP-018)

The evidence above is not a documentation deliverable. It is the durable
reasoning state a bounded actor needs, because the actor selecting a local
action generally does not hold the reasoning that produced the governing
frames. Dialogue, commentary, prior-agent memory and implementation
folklore are not that state (P0, P4b). The general
reconstruction rule is [ACTIVATION §1 Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake); this
clause states what design evidence supplies to it.

Given an accepted material-frame basis, as determined by the material
semantic boundary definition (§5), and a proposed bounded action, the
selected method basis together with the accepted design is sufficient to
recover every governing relation in the action's causally closed affected
set, and to decide whether the action preserves, changes, duplicates or
violates each of those relations. The two inputs are distinct and neither
substitutes for the other: the selected method describes which relations
are required and how to reason about them; the accepted design supplies
the concrete invariant values. A design that restates method decision law
to satisfy this rule reproduces the local-method duplication this law
exists to remove (P1, P6).

| Decision | The action, against a governing relation | Core value |
|---|---|---|
| preserves | leaves the relation intact and operates inside it | `satisfied` |
| changes | alters the relation itself, and therefore re-enters at that relation before acceptance | `invalid_basis` |
| duplicates | establishes an equivalent path that is explicitly disposed as a constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation | `satisfied` |
| violates | contradicts the relation, or establishes an equivalent path that is left undisposed | `falsified` |

The boundary between changes and violates is the locus of acceptance, not
the size of the delta: an otherwise lawful change accepted inside the
acting frame rather than at the relation it changes is a violation. The
boundary between duplicates and violates is disposition, not equivalence:
an equivalent path is lawful when disposed and a defect when not (P4b,
P6). Sufficiency is bound to a declared action and its affected set; it is
not a claim over an unbounded space of possible future changes, and the
performance of any particular reviewer is not evidence either way (P0).

The four decisions are a refinement of the core result algebra
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). They answer what the
action does to one governing relation, and each maps to exactly one core
value for the predicate "the action is admissible in the acting frame on
the current governing basis"; the value travels with that predicate and
with the decision, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6). `preserves` and a
disposed `duplicates` leave the relation as accepted. For `changes`, the
relation itself must change at its own locus before the action can be
accepted, so the current governing basis cannot support accepting it in
the acting frame, as for the disposition `re_enter` of
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#disposition). For `violates`, the
contradiction or the undisposed equivalent path is the counterexample. An
evaluation that reaches none of the four decisions returns the core value
its cause selects, `indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot
decide, naming what would decide (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results); where the
cause is that the selected method basis and the accepted design do not
suffice, the case falsifies this law, as stated below. Purpose and material relation: a lawful change is
never read as a violation or as an action the acting frame may accept, and
a violation is never read as a re-entry (P4b, P6).

This obligation adds no artifact. It is satisfied through the Ontology
evidence, authority matrix, transformation-admission relation, frame
declaration, views and module mapping already required, and is a property
of that material rather than a separate package (P2). The law is false if,
for a declared bounded action, the accepted design does not expose a
governing relation in that action's causally closed affected set, or the
preserve, change, duplicate or violate decision cannot be reached from the
selected method basis and accepted design without conversation history,
commentary, prior-worker memory or implementation folklore. Where the
sufficiency of a boundary is tested, the test uses named cases with known
governing relations and expected decisions, evaluated with conversation
history, commentary, prior-worker memory and implementation folklore
withheld (P6; EVALUATION §3).

## 5. Acceptance

Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject;
recording it cannot widen it, and it exhausts only the instance and interval
it names (P6, P2).
A work item closes by the condition it stated, not by a reviewer's approval;
a reviewer result is an input to closure, never the closure. Green labels,
document counts, review counts and historical outcomes are not acceptance.
A human decision may be exercised directly or through an explicitly admitted
bounded proxy. What a proxy grant names is
[IDENTITY §6](IDENTITY.md#6-authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004)'s,
and what a proxy can never decide is
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)';
for acceptance, a change a proxy cannot make re-enters at its owning
relation ([ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)).

Where the subject is a successor, its acceptance evidence includes the
successor disposition record of [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
(STDO-UP-015), which states the law: the exact predecessor immutable cut
the successor evolves, and one semantic disposition for every predecessor
claim capable of affecting the successor. A claim whose disposition is
unresolved cannot be qualified and so cannot be accepted; how the record
is evaluated is [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015).
An intentionally removed disposition is a decision of the current Product
authority, and its record is that decision (P6, P3, P4b).

### When a finding blocks promotion

A finding is a defect a review reports against the exact claim it
evaluated (§4). Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act
over that finding (§4, Result and triage projection). This section is the
one statement of when a finding can block; profiles and work carriers
refer to it and add only their domain triggers.

A review verdict is bounded by the exact reviewed claim and its applicable
hard stops ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)). A
finding can block current promotion only when it:

1. falsifies that claim;
2. exposes competing or ambiguous authority on the claim's acceptance
   path;
3. violates applicable active authority, safety or retained accepted
   behaviour; or
4. establishes a material architectural decision with durable
   consequences that forecloses an admitted Product outcome.

These conditions are necessary. Which of them suffice is decided as
follows:

| Consumed condition | Effect on the current promotion boundary |
|---|---|
| a valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | the boundary blocks, whatever the assigned priority or the decision cutoff |
| any other finding meeting one of the four conditions | the decision owner decides blocking from the exact affected claim, the governed outcome or decision the work serves ([ACTIVATION §1, Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake)), the applicable hard stops and the Product-owned cutoff policy; below that cutoff no block follows mechanically, and an accepted residual is retained explicitly |
| a finding meeting none of the four conditions | it does not block |
| an observation outside the exact reviewed claim | repricing or re-entry input, returned as §4 states: by itself it does not widen the reviewed subject, block its bounded claim, or require a new ticket, artifact, review round or implementation increment |

Severity selects neither priority nor a block mechanically, and priority
neither erases severity nor waives a hard stop. The decision cutoff is the
adopting Product's policy; this member sets no cutoff (P6, P2). This law
applies at any promotion boundary; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#promotion-constraint-projection)
binds the Executive instance. Purpose and material relation: one owner
gives every review consumer the same blocking condition. A bounded review
does not block on observations outside its claim, while a non-waivable hard
stop still blocks.

## 2. Release identities

The release-publication context distinguishes (P3):

- Project Release Namespace: a stable repository-local key assigned by
  the Product release authority to one independently released source
  project;
- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and
  Git tree object selected for one cut;
- Candidate Source: the candidate source of FOUNDATIONS §2, the mutable
  source-project state constructing a possible successor;
- RC Branch: a mutable project-qualified carrier for the current
  candidate window;
- Immutable RC Cut: an annotated project-qualified Git tag plus its exact
  Product release subject (FOUNDATIONS §2), naming one published candidate
  and, once accepted, one released Product; it realises the release cut;
- Version-Line Selector: the mutable project-qualified tag alias naming
  the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for that project and
  version line; it realises the version-line selector of FOUNDATIONS §2;
  and
- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience
  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.

Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the
version-line selector may move. An immutable RC tag never moves (P3).

### Project-qualified Git refs

`<project>` is one explicit Project Release Namespace. It matches
`[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*`, contains no slash, is unique within the
release source, and remains stable for the continuing release line. It is
assigned by the Product release authority. A directory name, display name,
definition label, package name or matching version cannot infer or
reassign it (P3, P6).

A shared release source uses these exact ref shapes for every future
publication (P3):

```text
RC branch:              refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>
immutable RC cut tag:   refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>
version-line selector:  refs/tags/<project>/v<version>
release branch:         refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>
```

The short Git tag names are therefore `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>` and
`<project>/v<version>`. A shared release source does not publish a future
cut or selector under the unqualified `v<version>-rc.<n>` or `v<version>`
refs (P3).

A single-project release source may retain the unqualified ref profile
only while it has exactly one independently released project and its
release record declares that profile. Adding a second independently
released project requires project-qualified refs before either project
publishes another cut (P3).

## 3. Phases

The release process has three phases (P0, P3, P6):

1. mutable candidate construction;
2. immutable RC publication and monotonic version-line advancement; and
3. exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption.

There is no second final cut after an accepted RC. Publication immediately
makes the new highest ordinal discoverable through the version-line
selector; acceptance remains a verdict over the exact immutable RC rather
than a second carrier. If any byte capable of affecting the Product or a
release-scoped claim changes, the project publishes and reviews a higher
immutable RC cut instead (P3, P6).
